name: devShark
tagline: Learn web development with graded quizzes, 770 server-graded coding tasks and a streak that forgives you.
description: devShark (devshark.app) is a one-developer learning platform for web developers: guided Learn paths, a public question of the day (/daily), 1,974 served quiz questions, 770 coding tasks graded on the server (JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Algorithms, system design), the Biggest Shark Challenge, a typing racer, forgiving streaks, 30-day leaderboards and an optional GitHub garden. Freemium since 25 Sep 2026: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React 1–12 and 116 of 770 tasks are free; Premium is 3.99 €/month or 39.99 €/year VAT included. Launch on social Sun 4 Oct 2026 with a launch price of 1.80 €/month or 18.00 €/year — 55 % below the regular price that applies from 3 Nov 2026 — kept for the lifetime of the subscription for everyone who subscribes by 2 Nov 2026, 23:59 CET.
audience: English-speaking self-taught and junior web developers (18–34) preparing for a first frontend/fullstack job or moving into React/TypeScript; they follow dev-education accounts (freeCodeCamp, roadmap.sh, Boot.dev, JavaScript Mastery, Fireship, Kevin Powell) on Instagram and Threads, save carousels, answer quiz posts and reply on Threads. Global, US-heavy, with the UK, India and the EU as large slices; Czech devs secondary (FrontKon Prague 5–6 Oct).
goal: Launch devShark on Threads and Instagram on 4 Oct 2026 and grow followers from zero with daily learning content, while the whole month promotes the launch price (Premium at 1.80 €/month or 18.00 €/year — 55 % below the regular 3.99 €/39.99 € that applies from 3 Nov 2026 — kept for the lifetime of the subscription; offer ends 2 Nov 23:59 CET).

Why profile visits and not traffic to /premium: the primary goal is followers; a cold dev audience rarely pays on the first click (35 € of traffic ≈ 20–70 /premium visits, too few to read a conversion); a profile visit lands on a grid whose pin #1 is the offer and whose bio links /premium?…launch-55, so the offer is seen without putting price claims in the ad.
ads.policyNotes: The chosen creative carries no price or discount claim, which avoids Meta's misleading-claims review of reference prices (Meta reviews the landing page against any price in an ad).
